item.title: Stranger Things Season 5 finale reactions: Fans call ending predictable, emotional and disappointing
item.description: After nearly a decade, Stranger Things ends with a finale that has left fans sharply divided. Some praised its emotional closure and character focus, others criticised its predictability, pacing, and unresolved arcs. The result is an ending that feels less definitive than debated, prompting arguments about risk, payoff, and what this story ultimately chose to prioritise.

item.title: ‘Took $50k while earning $750,000’: Anti-H1B influencer calls Vivek Ramaswamy a ‘fraud’
item.description: In a recent campaign trail clash, Republican gubernatorial contender Casey Putsch has taken aim at Vivek Ramaswamy, alleging that the wealthy entrepreneur accepted a $50,000 scholarship intended for underprivileged youth. This backlash follows Ramaswamy's defense of the fellowship during a 2023 interview, which he deemed "free money," despite his substantial earnings and his later stance against aid based on identity.

item.title: Chamath Palihapitiya? Sri Lankan-born billionaire thinking of leaving California for Texas
item.description: Chamath Palihapitiya is seriously considering a move away from California, prompted by emerging tax regulations. This decision echoes a growing sentiment among affluent entrepreneurs who are increasingly wary of the state's economic environment, particularly in light of a proposed 5% wealth tax on fortunes exceeding $1 billion.

item.title: ‘I’m going to...’: Filmmaker Mira Nair reacts to son Zohran Mamdani’s swearing-in as NYC mayor
item.description: In a groundbreaking political shift, Zohran Mamdani, the son of renowned filmmaker Mira Nair, stepped into history as the 112th mayor of New York City, taking his oath on the Quran. At just 34, this socialist democrat, shaped by his family’s rich heritage, ran a campaign advocating for universal childcare and a fairer tax on the affluent.

item.title: Popular Twitch creator Jynxzi hits massive milestone after streaming every day of 2025
item.description: Popular Twitch streamer Jynxzi has achieved a remarkable feat by streaming live every single day of 2025. This year-long challenge, completed without a single missed day, highlights his dedication, passion, and hard work. The accomplishment has garnered significant attention in the online world, reinforcing Jynxzi's commitment to his audience and his brand.

item.title: Was Markie Markland arrested in New York? Court and jail records spark buzz as influencer stays quiet
item.description: Online jail and court records show that Jovian “Markie” Markland was arrested in New York on December 29, 2025, and is held at the Eric M. Taylor Center. Court records confirm a Queens Criminal Court appearance and a January 13 hearing. Claims of fraud are unproven, with no official charges listed so far.

item.title: Watch: Kristi Noem and Stephen Miller dancing to ‘Ice Ice Baby’ leaves the internet cringing hard
item.description: South Dakota Governor Kristi Noem and White House advisor Stephen Miller faced online criticism after a video surfaced of them dancing and rapping to Vanilla Ice's "Ice Ice Baby" at Donald Trump's New Year's Eve party. The clip, shared by Miller's wife, sparked widespread embarrassment and mockery from netizens, highlighting their roles in the Trump administration's immigration policies.

item.title: 'Worst tragedy': Swiss president on fire that killed 40 in bar fire; flags to fly at half-mast for 5 days
item.description: A devastating fire ripped through Le Constellation bar in Crans-Montana during New Year celebrations. At least 40 people lost their lives and 115 were injured. Swiss President Guy Parmelin called it one of the country's worst tragedies. Authorities are investigating the exact circumstances of the blaze. Emergency operations are ongoing as the nation mourns.

item.title: Viral Instagram reel explains why British empire was built on gin and tonic
item.description: A viral clip of Sir Percy de Courcy dramatizes a truth long forgotten: gin and tonic was once vital medicine. Quinine in tonic warded off malaria, citrus prevented scurvy, and gin made it drinkable. More than a cocktail, it was a daily imperial tool, helping Britain maintain its tropical posts and safeguard personnel where disease, more than war, threatened empire.
